Wolfe Research's senior analyst Doug Leggate upgraded Chevron (CVX) shares to "Outperform" on July 2, announcing a $210 price target that represents significant upside from current levels. Subscribe today! Chevron stock advanced 1.6% on the day of the upgrade, though it remains well below its 52-week high of nearly $212. The central thesis behind the upgrade rests on a valuation disconnect between what the market is pricing in and CVX stock's improving fundamentals. Leggate argues that commodity price volatility has obscured genuine improvements in Chevron's sustainable cash generation capabilities. He contends that the market is currently embedding a long-term Brent oil price assumption below $60 a barrel, which is substantially lower than the normalized forward pricing curve of about $70 per barrel. This gap between implied and expected pricing creates what Leggate views as a compelling entry point for investors willing to look beyond near-term oil market noise. Guyana serves as the most critical near-term growth catalyst in the upgrade thesis. The Uaru development is expected to commence operations and reach a free cash flow inflection point during the second half of 2026, which should bolster Chevron's financial resilience even in a subdued oil price environment. Over time, Leggate expects Guyana to generate sufficient cash flow to offset dividend obligations tied to the Hess acquisition and eventually become CVX's "single largest contributor" to free cash flow. The strategic importance of Guyana intensifies as 2033 approaches, when the Tengiz partnership in Kazakhstan reaches its contractual conclusion. Beyond Guyana, Chevron has secured new development opportunities in 2026 across Venezuela, Libya, and Iraq, with a potential ninth Guyana development phase also under consideration. Wolfe Research believes these initiatives could sustain production growth well beyond the end of this decade, providing multi-year visibility into Chevron's growth trajectory. The broader analyst community remains predominantly bullish on CVX shares. The stock carries a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating with a mean price target of $216 across 25 analysts, comprising 19 "Buy," five "Hold," and one "Sell" rating. From a technical and valuation standpoint, Chevron Corp is approaching oversold territory with the relative strength index (RSI) currently hovering in the mid-30s. CVX's most recent quarterly earnings exceeded expectations by $0.41, delivering $1.41 per share versus a $1.00 consensus, and the upcoming Q2 earnings announcement is already being flagged as the next potential catalyst. However, the macro backdrop presents headwinds, with Brent crude having fallen to about $72 per barrel amid recovering Strait of Hormuz traffic, an OPEC+ production increase of 188,000 barrels per day for August, and concerns about a structural oil surplus that could pressure energy sector earnings in the near term. title: Flutter Entertainment (NASDAQ: FLUT), Lululemon (NASDAQ: LULU), And Chevron (NYSE: CVX): Cash Producers Worth Watching And One To Avoid - foreignpolicyjournal.com
content: By Ewan Scott | Jul 5, 2026 | Economy & Business, Featured, News & Analysis Strong free cash flow is widely regarded as a hallmark of business quality, but high cash generation alone does not guarantee market-beating returns for investors. Some cash-heavy companies struggle with inefficient capital allocation, weakening demand, or deteriorating competitive positioning that erodes long-term value. Flutter Entertainment (NASDAQ: FLUT), the global online sports betting and gaming giant behind FanDuel, PokerStars, Paddy Power, and Sky Betting and Gaming, is one name analysts suggest avoiding despite its scale. Flutter’s trailing 12-month free cash flow margin sits at just 3.7%, a figure that limits its ability to reinvest in growth, repurchase shares, or return meaningful capital to shareholders. The company posted annual revenue growth of 17.8% over the last two years, which fell below the benchmark standard for the consumer discretionary sector given its already large revenue base. Flutter’s subpar operating margin of 2.7% further constrains its capacity to respond to new competitive threats or fund meaningful operational improvements. The stock currently trades at $106.06 per share, implying a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 16.2x, a valuation that appears difficult to justify given the underlying financial profile. On the more favorable side of the ledger, Lululemon (NASDAQ: LULU) stands out as a compelling cash-producing business, carrying a trailing 12-month free cash flow margin of 11.4%. The athletic apparel retailer has demonstrated pricing power and product differentiation that support a best-in-class gross margin of 57.5%, a figure that reflects strong consumer demand for its offerings. Lululemon’s disciplined cost management has produced a two-year average operating margin of 20.8%, and the company continues to aggressively expand its store footprint into new markets. At $118.03 per share and a forward P/E of 10.4x, Lululemon presents a valuation that looks attractive relative to its operational strength and growth trajectory. Chevron (NYSE: CVX), the integrated energy giant with operations spanning deepwater drilling to retail fuel stations, rounds out the watchlist with a trailing 12-month free cash flow margin of 7.3%. Chevron has delivered above-market annual sales growth of 4.1% over the past decade, a notable achievement for a company operating at the scale of $190 billion in annual revenue. That dominant market position provides meaningful fixed-cost leverage as sales expand, allowing the company to generate cash well above what many of its industry peers can achieve. With a 10.4% free cash flow margin exceeding peer averages, Chevron retains considerable flexibility to reinvest in operations or return capital to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. The stock trades at $168.95 per share on a forward P/E of 10x, a valuation that reflects both the cyclical nature of energy markets and the company’s enduring competitive advantages in the sector. Ewan is a reporter at the Foreign Policy Journal, primarily covering US current affairs and news related to NYSE-listed stocks. He has over two decades of experience in journalism and digital publishing.

title: Chevron vs. Exxon Mobil: Which Energy Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026? - The Globe and Mail
content: Chevron is focusing on U.S. shale and new energy demand from the technology sector. Exxon Mobil is leveraging its massive global scale to lead in carbon capture and storage. Which oil giant represents the more compelling value for your portfolio today? Chevron(NYSE:CVX) and Exxon Mobil(NYSE:XOM) are titans of the global energy landscape, but their diverging paths in a changing economy present a unique puzzle for retail investors today. This match-up explores which stock is a better buy. Chevron is doubling down on operational efficiency in major basins while eyeing the power-hungry technology sector. Exxon Mobil is leveraging its massive scale to dominate traditional markets and lead the charge in carbon capture and storage. Both are navigating a transition toward cleaner energy while maintaining robust oil and gas production. Chevron sells crude oil, natural gas, and refined products to industrial and consumer markets globally. The company operates in major regions like Kazakhstan, Australia, and the U.S. shale basins through partnerships with entities like Hess Midstream LP. While primarily focused on fossil fuels, the company also monitors developments in renewable energy stocks to stay competitive in a changing market. In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $184.4 billion, representing a decrease of approximately 4.6% from the previous year. The company reported net income of close to $12.3 billion for the same period, down from $17.7 billion in 2024. This resulted in a net margin of roughly 6.7%, which measures how much of every dollar of sales remains after all expenses are paid. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.3x. This ratio measures total debt against shareholder equity, and a lower number indicates a lighter debt load. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, was nearly 1.2x. Free cash flow for the year was close to $16.6 billion, representing the cash a company generates after accounting for capital expenditures. Exxon Mobil operates as an integrated energy giant across more than 56 countries. The business spans oil, natural gas, chemicals, and growing investments in carbon capture technologies and lower-emission solutions. It maintains a diversified customer base across industrial and retail sectors without relying on any single customer concentration for more than 10% of revenue. For FY 2025, the company generated revenue of nearly $323.9 billion, a decline of about 4.5% compared to the prior year. Net income for the period was close to $28.8 billion, which was lower than the $33.7 billion earned in 2024. The company achieved a net margin of approximately 8.9%, which reflects the percentage of revenue turned into profit after all costs are considered. As of December 2025, the company’s debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.2x. This indicates that for every dollar of equity, the company carries close to 20 cents in total debt. The current ratio was approximately 1.2x, suggesting the company has enough liquid assets to cover its upcoming bills. Free cash flow for the year reached $26.1 billion, which is the cash left over after paying for maintenance and expansion of physical assets. Chevron faces significant sensitivity to fluctuations in global crude oil and natural gas prices. The integration of its acquisition of Hess Corporation also presents execution risks, as failing to reach production targets could hurt financial results. Additionally, the company manages ongoing pressure from climate regulations and the physical threat of extreme weather events on its infrastructure. Exxon Mobil deals with similar commodity price volatility and evolving global environmental laws. The company is also making large bets on technologies like carbon capture and hydrogen, which carry the risk that these markets may not develop as quickly as expected. It competes with other global players like Shell and BP while navigating geopolitical instability and trade sanctions in various international markets. Both companies are well-run, generate substantial free cash flow, and have long track records of rewarding shareholders through thick and thin. There's no bad choice here, which makes the decision more about conviction than avoidance. That said, ExxonMobil has a few things working in its favor right now. Its Guyana operations are producing at record levels, the Permian Basin business keeps growing, and the company has a credible plan to structurally reduce costs over the next several years regardless of where oil prices go. It's also returning cash to shareholders at an impressive pace, with dividends and buybacks totaling over nine billion dollars in a single quarter. Chevron is executing well too, but faces a bit more near-term uncertainty given its Venezuela exposure and some ongoing legal headwinds. When two giants look this similar, production growth and cost discipline are the tiebreakers. And ExxonMobil edges ahead on both. title: Is Chevron (CVX) Stock a Bargain? Wolfe Research Thinks So - MEXC
content: Chevron (CVX) rose 1.6% on Thursday after Wolfe Research upgraded the stock to Outperform from Peer Perform, setting a $210 price target. The stock opened Friday at $169.06, well below its 52-week high of $214.71. Wolfe analyst Doug Leggate argues that commodity price volatility has masked real improvements in Chevron’s long-term cash flow picture. The market, he says, is pricing in a long-term Brent oil price below $60 per barrel — well under the normalized forward curve of around $70. RBC Capital also reaffirmed its Buy rating on CVX this week, adding to the broadly positive analyst tone. The stock currently holds a consensus Moderate Buy rating with an average price target of $205.71 across 26 analysts — 19 Buy, 6 Hold, and 1 Sell. Mizuho raised its target from $225 to $230 in late May. Goldman Sachs and UBS both carry Buy ratings with targets of $216 and higher. Leggate points to Guyana as the most important near-term catalyst. The Uaru project is expected to start up and reach a free cash flow inflection point in the second half of 2026, which should improve CVX’s resilience if oil prices stay soft. Guyana is also expected to more than cover the dividends associated with the Hess acquisition — and over time, Leggate sees it becoming Chevron’s single largest contributor to free cash flow. That matters a lot heading into 2033, when the Tengiz contract in Kazakhstan is set to expire. Beyond Guyana, Chevron has secured new development opportunities this year in Venezuela, Libya, and Iraq, with a potential ninth phase of development in Guyana also on the table. These projects, Wolfe says, could extend production growth well beyond 2030. Institutional interest has picked up alongside the analyst upgrades. Peregrine Asset Advisers more than doubled its CVX position in Q1, growing its stake by 118.7% to 20,344 shares worth around $4.21 million. CVX last reported earnings on May 1st, posting $1.41 EPS against a consensus estimate of $1.00 — a beat of $0.41. Revenue came in at $47.56 billion, up 2.1% year-over-year, though slightly below the $51.86 billion analyst estimate. The company paid a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share in June, equating to a $7.12 annualized dividend and a 4.2% yield. The payout ratio currently sits at 123.4%. CVX’s Q2 2026 earnings conference call is scheduled later this month, which analysts are already flagging as the next potential catalyst for the stock. content: U.S. stock markets closed Friday because the New York Stock Exchange put July 3 down as the observed Independence Day holiday for 2026. Chevron Corporation NYSE:CVX only had four trading sessions this week, with Thursday’s action standing out more. Reuters said Friday analysts polled by LSEG see Chevron bringing in around $9.9 billion in adjusted net income for the second quarter—over three times its first-quarter result. With a market cap of about $336 billion as of Thursday, that’s a one-quarter profit yield of 2.9%. Exxon is on track for $15.9 billion, up against a $568 billion market cap, which puts its yield at 2.8%. This is notable since Chevron is trading like it’s set for a solid quarter, but shares didn’t get a boost this week. The market looks to be splitting how it values cash flow and risk. Oil has eased back, pump prices are under the political microscope, and the company’s new power segment is still something for 2028. Brent futures traded at $71.94 a barrel Friday afternoon, up 14 cents for the session and 5 cents under last Friday’s close. West Texas Intermediate was at $68.78. The company expects the site to reach up to 2.67 GW, starting operations in 2028. GE Vernova NYSE:GEV and Caterpillar NYSE:CAT gear are set for use, Chevron said.
